scope: Source-selected longer chains across Go, Python, Java, TypeScript and Rust. All repository graphs and older questions have been observed. No graph route inspected to choose these endpoint pairs.
endpointResolution: One public resolver per endpoint/tool. Both selectors validate identical symbol, file and declaration line. Compass search_symbols exact=true with source_file/start_line and old 256/500/524288 bounds; Graphify get_node file::symbol, validate source coordinate afterward. No graph ID substitution, retries or relaxed anchors. No kind filter.
bounds: Same 60 second deadline and 16 MiB per CLI stream, 1 MiB MCP response. Compass depth 8 and one path; Graphify has no matching depth flag. No equal-work or latency claim.
judgment: A complete directed call chain must identify the source declarations and each edge orientation/occurrence in the graph and source. Endpoint echoes, candidate lists, disconnected edges, or a reversed route do not count. Registered route is a positive witness, not a requirement to choose the same shortest route; independently source-review any alternate returned route.
reverse: Diagnostic probes only. The forward source witness does not prove global reverse unreachability. No-path/ambiguous/limit answers receive no absence credit. Review any returned reverse route for actual directed source support.
diagnostics: Compass max_depth 1 through one below the registered primary witness hops. Any alternate returned path must be source reviewed; never score it wrong solely for differing from witness. Retain overload/label ambiguity and mixed-relation routes as unmet call-path tasks. Do not assert shortest source paths from witnesses.
confidence: Source-supported inferred edges may be recorded as such; neither tool gets exact-evidence credit for weak/unknown confidence.
verification: Verify source revision, clean checkouts, source anchors and file digests, all graph/binary/environment hashes before and after. Preserve every output and every failure. Commit registration before running these endpoint pairs.
limitations: Five known development repositories; no held-out confirmation.
Endpoint assistance is part of workflow cost and differs from free-text question answering.
Source-supported static calls need not run on every invocation.
God-object design judgments, authored explanations and broader community/path quality remain unproven.
